newsitem.title: USA: Ill. agency gives final OK for Allstate bond plan.
newsitem.headline: Ill. agency gives final OK for Allstate bond plan.

text.p: The Illinois Development Finance Authority gave its final approval Wednesday to enter into an agreement with Allstate Insurance Co, a unit of Allstate Corp, for a non-profit bond program.

Bobby Wilkerson, the authority's director, said the approval puts a conceptual program in place so that the agency, Allstate and the Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar's office can review upcoming bond proposals.
Elio Montenegro, a spokesman for Northbrook, Ill.-based Allstate, said the board's action gives the insurer the "green light to go ahead and work out more specific plans."
"We're excited about this project," he added.
The program was only changed slightly by Allstate since the agency's board last month informally voiced its support for the program, according to authority officials.

Under the innovative program, Allstate would participate in a public/private relationship allowing it to purchase bonds of social service agencies in Illinois with limited credit enhancement provided by the authority.

The aim of the program is to give social service agencies that are largely dependent on state contracts for their funding acess to the debt market at lower costs by eliminating the need for a letter of credit or bond insurance.
Wilkerson said a $15 million tax-exempt bond deal proposed by CARES, a group of agencies on Chicago's southside, is expected to be the first to come before the board perhaps in April.
